key_insight: AlB₁₂–Al detonation coatings improved the wear resistance of steel 45, with AB70 showing more stable tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: The coatings offer a potential route to protecting steel components exposed to sliding wear.
method: Deposited AB70 (70 wt.% AlB₁₂, 30 wt.% Al) and AB30 (30 wt.% AlB₁₂, 70 wt.% Al) using a DNEPR-5M detonation system.
Characterized coating thickness, hardness and surface structure.
Evaluated friction and wear under varying sliding speeds and loads.
evidence_signal: Coatings were approximately 170–200 μm thick; AB70 exhibited friction coefficients of 0.21–0.38 and wear rates of 3.3–8.6 μm/km, while coated samples outperformed uncoated steel 45 in wear resistance.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify test loads, sliding speeds or statistical uncertainty, limiting assessment of service-condition applicability.
paper_title: Structure and properties of AlB12-Al detonation coatings on steel 45
